ocr.notes: Transcript is only the caption and a few line fragments. The facts below were read from the full-resolution page image.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen would marry Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove, 21, the English-born trained nurse who had attended him through several months of illness, on April 23, his 65th birthday.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, March 28, 1903, page 3. Duplicate of article 1000.

facts.fact: Allen announced on March 27, 1903 that he would marry Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove, 21, a trained nurse who had been attending him in an illness of several months, on April 23, his 65th birthday
Mrs. Hartgrove, like Allen a native of England, was born in Manchester and came to St. Louis at the age of 9
The paper said Allen had been a widower for thirty years and his future wife a widow for about two years
The paper said Allen's first battle was with Charlie Davis on April 17, 1878, whom he beat in five rounds for the championship of England

Allen's fight with Mike McCool for the American championship, with a $2,000 purse, was announced to take place in St. Louis but stopped by police; the party chartered a steamer up the Mississippi to Gabaret Island, where it was fought out of doors
Allen had been confined since Christmas 1902 with a chronic malady at the home of his sister-in-law, 3516 Arsenal Street, and was to be moved to the Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues
places: Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis

notes: Duplicate of article 1000 (same story, same page) with a far worse crop; consider removing 1001 or merging it into 1000. If kept, recrop to the full story (two-column headline, first column, and continuation in the second column above 'Apple Mary's Wedding'). Contradictions: 'first battle' with Davis in 1878 is wrong for his career; 'widower for thirty years' vs 1004's 'left a wife' in England (index 040); Hartgrove 'a widow' vs her divorce suit (1003); 65th birthday implies 1838, vs 1839 elsewhere.
